paras: A curious 11‑year‑old in Melbourne hears about US politics. President Donald Trump had picked Heidi Overton to run the Food and Drug Administration. Soon after, Trump changed his mind and asked her to step down.

news.title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
paras: No Starshield, no problem Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits Ukraine’s strike used homegrown tech while adapting battlefield lessons from its adversary. Vantor satellite image shows multiple smoke generator vehicles obscuring part of the Crimea Bridge crossing over the Kerch Strait on June 22, 2026.

Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times .

news.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
paras: Hardened Defaults Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security Hardened defaults align with DoD standards, but there may be growing pains. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).

STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default.

news.title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
paras: Republicans are unanimous Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote Democrats try to prevent quorum, say Thumann lied about not working on media issues. Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) at a hearing on Tuesday, January 28, 2025.

Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote. All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee’s 13 Democrats were absent. “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” Cruz said at today’s hearing.

news.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet los
paras: Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN.

The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars .

news.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
paras: The answer to one of Earth's greatest geological mysteries may lie deep beneath our feet. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past.

Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Watch full video here: Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years.

news.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
paras: As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star.

However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. news.title: A Gene Variant Inherited From Neanderthals Might Affect Modern Humans' Brain Size and Provide Protection Again
paras: Add as preferred source Most humans alive today carry a bit of Neanderthal DNA. Mike Kemp / In Pictures via Getty Images Tens of thousands of years ago, Homo sapiens interbred with Neanderthals , resulting in billions of humans alive today carrying traces of these extinct cousins in their DNA.

The bits of Neanderthal ancestry can affect mood, metabolism, disease risk and other traits . Now, new research suggests one of those inherited genetic variants is associated with a slightly shrunken brain region and lower risk of schizophrenia, according to a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on November 16.

sport.title: Rennae Stubbs responds when asked if Serena Williams will return to tennis in 2027
paras: After months of speculation, the 23-time major singles champion returned to the court at the Queen’s Club Championships, playing alongside Victoria Mboko in the doubles event. It was a successful return to competitive play for the American – she and Mboko defeated third seeds Erin Routliffe and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 7-6, 6-2.

The duo were forced to withdraw from their next match following Mboko’s season-ending injury. Serena made her return to singles play a short while later, losing to Australian youngster Maya Joint in the Wimbledon first round. The 45-year-old has not played a singles match since making an appearance at the All England Club.

sport.title: The five active players who have won the most matches at the ATP Finals in their careers
paras: Alexander Zverev secured his place in the ATP Finals semi-finals after defeating Ben Shelton on Tuesday evening. It was a superb performance by the German, who triumphed 6-2, 7-6 inside the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy.

Zverev clearly has Shelton’s number on the ATP circuit, as evidenced by his 7-0 head-to-head record against the 23-year-old American. Zverev has been one of the most successful players at the ATP Finals over the last decade, winning two titles – in 2018 and 2021 – and reaching the semi-finals at multiple editions of the event.

sport.title: “The saddest match of my career”: Cobolli fights back tears after his Turin exit
paras: Anyone who has spent time around Flavio Cobolli knows the Italian is all in: generous, wholehearted, fully committed to his tennis dream. “This is definitely the match that makes me the saddest of my career,” the Italian said quietly.

The world No 6, a Roland-Garros finalist this year, is out of the ATP Finals in Turin on his debut, at home, without winning a set. The question that brought him close to tears was not about the match but about his season. He asked for it to be repeated, seemingly to buy time.

sport.title: Frances Tiafoe Downs Lacklustre Cobolli To Keep ATP Finals Dream Alive
paras: Frances Tiafoe overcame a sluggish start to his latest match at the ATP Finals to defeat a misfiring Flavio Cobolli in straight sets. The world No.8 fought his way through a roller-coaster opening set before sealing a 7-6(6), 6-0 victory at the season-ending event, which he is playing for the first time in his career.

It is only the second time Tiafoe has won an indoor match this season. He is the fourth American to win at least one match at the ATP Finals since 2010 after Taylor Fritz (6), Jack Sock (2) and Ben Shelton (1).

sport.title: “That was pretty brutal”: Tiafoe silences Turin to crush Cobolli, Alcaraz tops group
paras: Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0 on Wednesday night at the ATP Finals in Turin, his first win at the event. The result sends Carlos Alcaraz through as winner of the Ivan Lendl Group, knocks out the home favourite and turns Friday’s Medvedev-Tiafoe match into a quarter-final in all but name.

There are nights when the silver “Big Foe” chain around Frances Tiafoe ’s neck shines brighter than others, and Wednesday at the Inalpi Arena was one of them. The American earned the first win of his career at the ATP Finals, beating Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0 in 1 hour and 32 minutes, with tennis of rare precision against an opponent who was knocked out in the second set.
